questions.question: Which among the following period of the stone age **first** witnessed the domestication of animals?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Mesolithic Age__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Mesolithic Age falls roughly from **9000 B.C. to 4000 B.C**.
 
• It was the transitional phase between the Paleolithic Age and Neolithic Age.
 
• Although Mesolithic men were still dependent largely on hunting, now they used began **taming the animals** like dog, sheep, goat, cow-ox, buffalo, wild horse, etc.
 
• The earliest evidence of the taming of animals was found from **Adamgarh of Madhya Pradesh** and **Baghore of Rajasthan**. They are Mesolithic sites. **Hence, Option 4 is correct**.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Paleolithic: 

 
 
• It is the earliest Stone age period dating 2.6 million years ago.
 
• The age is distinguished by most primitive stone tools. Humans during the era grouped together in small “bands” and were involved in gathering plants, fishing, and hunting.
 
• The paleolithic period is the longest in human history.
 
• The age can be divided into lower Paleolithic, Middle Paleolithic, and Upper Paleolithic. 
 
• During the end of the age, people developed spiritual and religious beliefs as depicted in some of the excavations.
 
 
 
• Mesolithic: It is the second period of the stone age between Paleolithic and Neolithic. The start and end of the age vary by geographical region. It is a transition period from hunting and gathering as in Paleolithic to domestication as in Neolithic. The tools used were the mode V chipped stone tools (microliths).
 
• Neolithic: It is the 3rd period of the stone age and is often referred to as the “New stone age”. Its time period is considered to be around 10,200 BC to 4,500BC, which ended with the beginning of the “Bronze Age”.
 
• **Microlith**: It is a small tool made up of flint or chert, used to form the points of hunting weapons.

questions.question: Which of the following statement is correct regarding the Neolithic period?

options.text: The people during this period were predominantly hunters and gatherers.
The domestication of animals was not known during this period.
The pottery was not known to the people during this period.
The period is significant for its megalithic architecture.

questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is __**Option 4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

Neolithic Age:

 
• **The Neolithic Age saw the man turning into food products from food gatherer. It also witnessed the use of pottery for the first time**. People used microlithic blades in addition to tools made of polished stone. The use of metal was unknown. **Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.**
 
• **Agriculture:** The people of the Neolithic Age cultivated ragi, horse gram, cotton, rice, wheat, and barley and hence were termed as food producers. They domesticated cattle, sheep, and goats. Agriculture and animal domestication were the main economic activity of early Neolithic cultures. **Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.**
 
• **Tools:** The people used microlithic blades in addition to tools made of polished stones. They used stone hoes and digging sticks for digging the ground. They also used tools and weapons made of bone; found in Burzahom (Kashmir) and Chirand (Bihar).
 
• **Weapons: **The people primarily used axes as weapons. The North-western part of the Neolithic settlement used rectangular axes having curved cutting edge. The Southern part used axes with oval sides and pointed butt while polished stone axes with rectangular butt and shouldered hoes used in the north-eastern part.
 
• **Housing:** The people of the Neolithic Age lived in rectangular or circular houses which were made of mud and reed. The people of Mehrgarh lived in mud-brick houses while pit-dwelling is reported from Burzahom, the Neolithic site found in Kashmir.
 
• **Pottery: The pottery first appeared in the Neolithic Age**. The pottery of the period was classified under grey ware, black-burnished ware, and mat-impressed ware. **Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.**
 
• **Architecture:** **The Neolithic Age is significant for its Megalithic Architecture**. **Hence, statement 4 is correct.**
 
• **Technology:** In the initial stage of the Neolithic Age, hand-made pottery was made but later on the foot-wheels were used to make pots.
 
• **Community Life:** Neolithic people had common rights over the property. They led a settled life.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding Old Stone Age:

1. The period is divided into Lower Palaeolithic culture, Middle Palaeolithic culture, Upper Palaeolithic culture and Final Palaeolithic culture.

2. The period after the Old Stone Age is called the Neolithic Age.

Which among the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Neither 1 nor 2**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****Old Stone Age:**

__
 
• The earliest age in history is called** Old Stone Age or Palaeolithic.**
 
• This period is divided into-
 
 
• Lower Palaeolithic culture
 
• Middle Palaeolithic culture
 
• Upper Palaeolithic culture . ***Hence, statement 1 is not correct.***
 
 
 
• **The period after the Old Stone Age (Palaeolithic) is called the Mesolithic Age**.*** Hence, statement 2 is not correct.***
 
• The period that followed the **Mesolithic is called the Neolithic Age.**
 
• This is the age in which **animal and plant domestication **developed, leading to food production.
 
• The classification of these cultures is done **on the basis of stratigraphic, chronological and lithic (stone tool) evidence.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**Lower Palaeolithic Culture:

 
• The first Palaeolithic tools were** identified at the site of Pallavaram** near Chennai by Robert Bruce Foote in 1863.
 
• Robert found many** prehistoric sites when he extensively surveyed** different parts of South India.

**Middle Palaeolithic Culture:**

 
• In India, the **Middle Palaeolithic phase** was first identified by **H.D. Sankalia on the Pravara River at Nevasa.**
 
• Indian Middle Palaeolithic is probably maybe as old as the African Middle Palaeolithic culture.

**Upper Palaeolithic Culture:** 

 
• This period is marked by** innovation in tool technology** and increased cognitive capability of humans.

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding the Social and economical life of Harappan Culture is correct?

options.text: Beads were worn by women only.
The use of cosmetics was common.
The Harappans did not carried trade in stone, metal, shell,
The Harappan people did not know about cotton.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The use of cosmetics was common.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Beads were worn by women and men.**

 
 
• ​Hence statement 1 is not correct.
 
 
 
• **The use of cosmetics was common.**
 
 
• ​Hence statement 2 is correct.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Economy

 
 
• The importance of trade in the life of the Indus people is witnessed by the presence of numerous seals, uniform script, and regulated weights and measures in a wide area.
 
• The Harappans carried on a considerable trade in stone, metal, shell, etc. *Hence statement 3 is not correct.*
 
• Metal money was not used and trade was carried by the barter system.
 
 
 
• **Agriculture**
 
 
• **The Harappan villages, mostly situated near the flood plains, produced sufficient foodgrains.**
 
• **Wheat, barley, rai, peas, sesame, lentil, chickpea, and mustard were produced**.
 
 
• Millets are also found at sites in Gujarat. While rice uses were relatively rare.
 
 
 
• The Harappan people were the earliest people to produce cotton. ​***Hence statement 4 is not correct.***
 
• While the prevalence of **agriculture **is indicated by finds of grain, it is more difficult to reconstruct actual agricultural practices.
 
• **Traces of canals have been found at the Harappan site of Shortughai in Afghanistan, but not in Punjab or Sindh.**
 
 

39:T

questions.question: The earliest evidence for the making and use of stone tools comes from sites in _________
questions.solution:
The earliest evidence for the making and use of stone tools comes from sites in **__Ethiopia and Kenya__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **earliest evidence for the making and use of stone tools** comes from sites in **Ethiopia and Kenya**, and dates back to at least 2.6 million years ago.
 
• These tools are known as **Oldowan tool**s, and they are characterized by their simple, flaked-stone design.
 
• Oldowan tools were likely used for a variety of purposes, including butchering meat, processing plants, and digging.
 
• It is likely that the earliest stone tool makers were the **Australopithecus.**
 
• Here are some of the most important archaeological sites in Ethiopia and Kenya that have yielded evidence of early stone tool use:
 
 
• **Omo Kibish**__: This site in Ethiopia is home to some of the oldest known stone tools, dating back to 2.6 million years ago.
 
• __**Gona**__: This site in Ethiopia is known for its large number of Oldowan tools.
 
• __**Lomekwi**__: This site in Kenya is home to some of the earliest known large cutting tools, dating back to 3.3 million years ago.
 
• **__Turkana West__**: This site in Kenya is known for its large number of well-made Oldowan tools.
 
 
 
• 
 
These sites provide important evidence of the early development of stone tool technology and the evolution of human behavior and cognition.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is __Ethiopia and Kenya__.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Burial Methods in Harappan Culture:

1. Complete burial and post-cremation burial were popular at Mohenjodaro.

2. At Lothal, the burial pit was lined with burnt bricks indicating the use of coffins.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both 1 and 2.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Complete burial and post-cremation burial were popular at **Mohenjodaro**.

 
 
• Hence statement 1 is correct.
 
 
 
• At **Lothal, **the burial pit was lined with burnt bricks indicating the use of coffins.
 
 
• Hence statement 2 is correct.
 
 
 
• **Wooden coffins** were also found at **Harappa.**
 
• The **practice of pot burials** is found at **Lothal** sometimes with pairs of skeletons.
 
• There is **no clear evidence for the practice of Sati.**​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ​Religion

 
 
• In Harappa, numerous terracotta figurines of women have been found. In one figurine a plant is shown growing out of the embryo of a woman.
 
• The Harappans, therefore, looked upon the earth as a fertility goddess and worshipped her in the same manner as the Egyptians worshipped the Nile goddess Isis.
 
• The male deity is represented on a seal with three-horned heads, represented in the sitting posture of a yogi.
 
• This god is surrounded by an elephant, a tiger, a rhinoceros, and has a buffalo below his throne. At his feet appear two deer.
 
 
• The depicted god is identified as **Pashupati Mahadeva.**
 
 
 
• Numerous symbols of the phallus and female sex organs made of stone have been found.
 
• The people of the Indus region also worshipped trees and Animals.
 
• The most important of them is the one-horned unicorn which may be identified with the rhinoceros and the next important was the humped bull.
 
• Amulets have also been found in large numbers.

questions.question: Which among the following Indus Valley Sites was discovered by Rakhal Das Bannerjee?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Mohenjodaro.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mohenjodaro, an ancient Indus Valley Civilization city was discovered in 1922 by R.D. Banerji (Rakhaldas Banerjee) who is an officer of the Archaeological Survey of India.**
 
• Large-scale excavations were carried out at this site under the direction of John Marshall, Ernest Mackay, K.N. Dikshit, and some others in the 1930s.
 
• Along with the Great Bath, the Great Granary was also present in Mohenjodaro.
 
• Mesopotamian seals and miniature pots of fiance were also found at the site.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kalibangan:**

 
 
• It is in the Hanumanghar district of Rajasthan, which is located near the banks of the river Ghaggar.
 
• It means black bangles, the black bangle factory remains were seen in this region.
 
• The leg bone of the elephant was found in Kali Bangan.
 
 
 
• **Harappan:**
 
 
• It is located in Sahiwal district, Punjab on the banks of the Ravi.
 
• It is excavated by Daya Ram Sahni.
 
 
 
• **Lothal:** 
 
 
• It is located in Gujarat on the Bhogva river near the Gulf of Cambay.
 
• It is excavated by R. Rao.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:

**Assertion (A):** Bhimbetka rock shelters were inhabited by hunter-gatherers.

**Reason (R):** The Narmada Valley provided essential resources, such as water and stones for tools

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

questions.solution:
**The correct answer is 'Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.'**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

 
• **Bhimbetka rock shelters and their significance:**

 
 
• Bhimbetka rock shelters, located in central India, are an important archaeological site that provides evidence of early human life.
 
• The shelters were inhabited by hunter-gatherers, as indicated by various archaeological findings, including tools and cave paintings.
 
 
 
• **Resources provided by the Narmada Valley:**
 
 
• The Narmada Valley, in which the Bhimbetka rock shelters are situated, offered essential resources that supported the hunter-gatherer lifestyle.
 
• Key resources included water from the Narmada River and stones that could be used to make tools.
 
• These resources facilitated the survival and daily activities of the inhabitants.
